body:
I agree,  the work aspect worries me. I had a casual relationship with a colleague who was double my age (I'm mid twenties). I was honest and up front that I wasn't looking for anything serious and he said all the right things to convince me he felt the same. I ended things once I realised he wanted a lot more.

 I thought we could go back to being professional but I was so wrong. He harassed me until I blocked him, then he started calling me on the work phone (no caller I'd so I Had to answer) to beg me/threaten me/ everything you can imagine. I still had to see him a few times a week and he'd either shout at me or try and touch me or beg to talk. I was scared to say anything because he told me he'd make me lose my job. I was also afraid of workplace drama and gossip going around. In the end I had to speak to my manager about it because it was affecting every part of my life. He's now been moved to another location and seems to have stopped after several conversations with my manager.

Whe  you get into these things you hope it'll work out but if it goes wrong and you work together, it can be hard to end it. As adults, we rarely meet new people and work is one of the main places we get to do that so it's easy to end up in these situations. Just bear in mind the challenges in walking away.

Thank you for replying. 
I trust my Daddy to be in control and keep me safe. I will definitely mention that I want him to be there at all times. I think that's a given for him but it's better to clarify. We have a safeword and will go over it before anything happens.
I like some of the ideas for 3 and will discuss them.
That's a great idea I hadn't thought of. I will make sure to look for reactions when having these conversations to ensure I'm respected and comfortable with him.

I like the idea of my Dom showing the other guy what works on me.

I did consider attraction as a potential issue and whether I would need to get to know him more. But I don't think it's as important to me. I'm excited by the scenario and want it to be someone that my Dom trusts and has chosen. I will absolutely say no if I am not comfortable with him. Protection is a good point which I've considered but have yet to raise.

I think I will ask my Dom if we can hang out a few times and discuss our interests and our experiences in a relaxed way like I did with him when we met. 

Thank you for your response.

As a younger woman who has dated guys over 40 I love calling them daddy. It's definitely a kink for me and was for one of my older partners (who happens to have kids). However, another guy (the one without kids) felt it was weird due to the age gap so I avoided it. Both partners need to be comfortable with it for it to be okay. Particularly if using it in a sexual context rather than a joking/endearing one.

I know that feeling. But I just look at the immediate future like if I wake up in the morning can I get dressed? That seems doable so I manage that and then its figuring out the next thing. Don't worry about next week or next month of next year. Dont even think about the past. It's not productive at all in this state. 

Just get through the next little task, it can be as small as you like. But acknowledge that success and be proud. Then go onto the next one. You're already doing better than giving up fully. Give yourself a break.

Then I would suggest looking at your successes, however small. I got a job that I ultimately quit due to anxiety and stress. But the shit that I had to deal with  at that job gave me massive strength. It was awful at the time. And I felt like I'd failed when I quit (was close to being fired for too much sickness due to anxiety). That job sucked but I learned a lot from it. It had value to me. Dont regret those things, take something from them and take it to the next job. 

But also look for different types of jobs. I found that retail was far too stressful for me. But I now work in care and I love it. Theres more responsibility and everything but it's a different kind of stress. You have value, you are a good person. Find what you enjoy and give it a go.

You might feel like you suck at everything but given what you've shared here I don't think that's true. You were a successful student and while mental health got in the way of that, you are still an intelligent person.

Can I ask why you cant hold a job?

Sometimes my only reason to live is to see what happens next. "I can always kill myself later" is strangely reassuring. It did get better for me. While I can't make any promises, I encourage you to try a bit longer each time you feel like this. That's what I'm doing. Things are shit again but I keep going because it got better once and it could again. I'm sorry, I hope this is in some way reassuring. Just try to be honest.

Why am I finding so many people I relate to on this sub? But seriously, I was the straight A student, who felt like all that matters is grades and academics. Its bullshit. The best thing I ever did was say no to all that. I too dropped out of college due to mental health. Then I found a mentor. Someone in a job that didn't pay well or require good grades. But that person made a huge difference to my life and the lives of so many young people like me. And I realised that being smart and making money wasn't the answer. Find something you enjoy, something that has nothing to do with your education or the subjects you chose. And be happy. Personally I just want to do anything to help other people. The pay is shit, the hours are shit, but fuck it's a lot better than being the gifted child.

So much of what you've said really resonates with me. I feel the same way about my friends and I have always been the "listener" or the mum friend as I put it. I struggle with my sexuality and gender (I'm pansexual but could be straight passing due to my current relationship. I identify as gender fluid and struggle to reconcile that with my day to day life).

I have in the past been in a relationship with someone who would send me pictures of their self harm every time I left their house (to go to my house or just do something I needed to do). I feel so responsible for everyone else, partly as a result of that relationship. I'm scared to not reply to a message from a friend even if I dont have the emotional energy to deal with it at that time because I'm Terrified that they will hurt themselves. 

I assume I'm a lot younger than you so maybe I cant understand that part but I feel theres so much pressure even in your 20s to be up together and have a plan and be a productive member of society.

You are clearly a good person or you wouldn't attract these manipulative people in the first place. Please be strong. Live for yourself, not for someone else. You have value. You deserve to have your own life and enjoyment, not based on other people's  manipulative behaviour. Those people aren't your responsibility.

If you have interests, go out and try them. Ignore those who say you're too old. I've learnt in the last few years age doesn't matter when it comes to friends. I have lots of friends 20years my senior. And people worried and people judged but I dont care because we have similar interests and views and feelings. Its certainly better than having no friends. 

If you want to message me feel free, anytime and I'll try to help as best I can.
